script.base: Market prices Washington to lead: implied totals about WAS 23.0 and PHI 17.5 in a 40.5 game. Base flow is WAS ahead by a score at half, moderate pace, second-half run lean behind J.Croskey-Merritt (20 carries, 97 yards in weeks 4-6) plus J.Daniels' legs, while PHI trails and throws into a 46% blitz. D.Pierce's recent carry share stalls; D.Goedert (24 targets, 147 yards over weeks 5-7) works the middle. Wind 5.1 and 49.6 F do not force a run-only or under script.
script.flip1: PHI hangs within a score or leads. They stay balanced, S.Barkley's 62 yards on only 7 carries (8.9 YPC) becomes a real workload, PHI rush unders get pressured, and Goedert's dropback volume drops because they are not in pass-to-catch-up mode. WAS never salts it away.
script.flip2: WAS scores early and leads by 14+. PHI abandons the run, backup rush lines die, and garbage throws can still feed Goedert. Or both offenses bog down — PHI QB is -0.23 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=96) and WAS is only +0.14 when not blitzed — and 40.5 goes under without a pass-volume spike.

Receiving leaders Okonkwo 17/134, Diggs 16/79, A.Williams 15/102, T.Burks 14/139; T.McLaurin only 6/89, so he has been the limited one recently. Who gains if that holds: Goedert and the WAS committee backs. Who loses: Mitchell's rush line, and deep PHI WRs if the 46% blitz gets home.

matchup.shell: Man/zone and MOFO/MOFC charting not in the pack. Location splits are the proxy. WAS allows middle 9.5 YPA (48 att), right 8.06 (93 att), left 5.15 (78 att) — middle open, left closed. PHI is flat: left 7.06 (79 att), middle 7.19 (59), right 7.1 (106).
matchup.pressure: WAS blitz rate 46% into a PHI QB at -0.23 EPA/dropback vs blitz (n=96) versus -0.03 unblitzed, so pressure should cut deep air yards (Smith 179, Wicks 171) and push checkdowns. PHI blitzes only 25%, which is the mode where the WAS QB is better (+0.14 EPA unblitzed vs -0.13 vs blitz, n=72).
matchup.bleeds: WAS bleeds the middle (9.5 YPA) and is ordinary vs the run (4.17 YPC, only 12 runs of 10+). PHI bleeds the run (4.31 YPC, 21 runs of 10+) and has no pass-direction hole; explosives allowed are 23 of 254 throws (about 9%), similar to WAS 20 of 230.
matchup.overlap: Goedert is the PHI primary target (24 targets, 147 yards, 115 air yards over three games) and WAS's weak spot is the middle, with a 46% blitz that the skill map sends to TE/RB checkdowns. That is the overlap. No WAS primary in the priced menu attacks a PHI hole the same way: PHI pass YPA is ~7.1 everywhere, and the soft PHI spot is the run, where Croskey-Merritt is not offered.

form: Avoid season averages; pack is L3 totals only, not game logs, so one-play inflation cannot be separated. Goedert 8.0 targets and 49.0 rec ypg, 6.1 yards per target, with Lemon close behind at 43.0 ypg — middle usage is stable, not a one-week spike. Smith 75 yards on 179 air yards is the failed deep profile. Mitchell 3 carries, 11 yards (3.7 ypg) behind Pierce 12.3 carries/game at a poor 2.6 YPC; Barkley 2.3 carries/game but 8.9 YPC, a tiny efficient sample, not a volume role. WAS: Burks 46.3 ypg on 75 air ypg vs a 21.5 line and Diggs 26.3 ypg on 5.3 targets vs a 42.5 line are role-or-efficiency conflicts the pack does not explain; Okonkwo 44.7 ypg vs 33.5 has no price. Daniels 38.3 rush ypg on 10.5 YPC is explosive form that should not be treated as a stable mean. White 15.0 rush ypg and 10.7 rec ypg vs rush 41 / rush+rec 58.5 is a market role upgrade the L3 committee (Croskey-Merritt, Daniels, Ekeler) does not show.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Goedert is Philadelphia's primary target at 24 targets and 147 yards over the last three, and Washington bleeds the middle at 9.5 YPA while blitzing 46 percent into a QB who is -0.23 EPA vs blitz, so 45.5 receiving yards is light if that checkdown overlap holds.
edge_players.must_be_true: Goedert plays a full route share, PHI dropbacks stay elevated in a trailing or garbage script, and he — not only Lemon — keeps the middle targets.
edge_players.kills_it: Blitz becomes sacks and three-and-outs instead of completions, WAS takes the TE away, or PHI leads and runs so his 8 targets/game never show up.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Mitchell has 3 carries for 11 yards in three games behind Pierce's 37, and a 5.5-point dog script should shrink PHI rush volume further, so 28.5 is a starter number on a third back.
edge_players.must_be_true: Pierce and Barkley are both active so Mitchell stays near one carry a game, and PHI does not hand him a surprise lead-back share.
edge_players.kills_it: A late scratch the pack does not list elevates him, or a competitive PHI lead plus 7-8 carries at WAS's 4.17 YPC allowed clears 28.5.

data_check.notes: No projection, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig in the pack, so step 8 cannot be priced beyond the posted juice. Form agrees with both sides: Goedert 49.0 ypg vs 45.5; Mitchell 3.7 ypg vs 28.5. WAS middle 9.5 YPA and 46% blitz agree with the Goedert read; nothing in the pack cuts it. PHI implied total 17.5 is a sizing caution, not a contradiction, because 45 yards is one-drive production. Do not treat either leg as a 70% model probability. Nan-priced board numbers (Okonkwo 33.5, Lemon 44, White rush 41, Williams 38, Hollywood Brown 22) were not used. Barkley rush under 44.5 and Burks over 21.5 were dropped as leans the posted lines disagree with via unexplained role pricing.

market_rung_price: dallasgoedert recyds over 45.5 -114; elijahmitchell rushyds under 28.5 -113. Main lines only; no alt rungs in the pack. Passing yards, receptions, and TDs excluded. No-vig not available, so juice is the American price as listed.
pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because the 46% blitz never became checkdowns: PHI's -0.23 EPA vs blitz showed up as sacks and three-and-outs, Goedert finished around 30 yards, and the middle 9.5 YPA went to Lemon instead of the TE, wiping a cushion of only 3.5 yards versus his 49 ypg. Mitchell cleared 28.5 because a scratch not in this pack gave him 8-9 carries in a game that stayed inside one score, so PHI never abandoned the run, and WAS's 4.17 YPC allowed was enough. The -5.5 script was wrong, weather was a non-factor, and the thin Goedert number lost to ordinary TE variance.
slip_story: One story only: WAS leads, PHI throws into the blitz, middle/TE volume up, PHI backup rush volume dead. Stack Goedert recyds over with Mitchell rushyds under. Do not add a total over, a PHI RB over, or a WAS shootout receiver. Croskey-Merritt would be the clock-killing correlate but he is not on the board. Two legs, no TDs, one market per player.
